column8: Fri 20 Nov: 3d, settles campaign director 2 and D8 with CASE's own counting rule (signed document: amount, purpose, payment period); read as quoted by Taylor 2021, the standards themselves paywalled.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of Q133-028 (only the entity with legal control can pledge); adds only Taylor's assuming-liability line and the 2021 edition.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d support; a CASE-style campaign policy: one written dollar amount and schedule, counted on receipt of the written pledge, so a spoken range counts for nothing.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, answers plain reader 12 and campaign 2 at source: oral pledges are not reported and the officer writes to document them; owned is not counted until written.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d letter checklist (date, amount, purpose, schedule, no condition); the no-condition point is already Q147's, the fields row 1's.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d parallel D8 asks for (plain reader 12): Spelman's we don't spend money unless we have it left it owing nothing when Lehman paid $3m of $10m; adds the quotes to H7-070.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, the promise broke in the gap between purchase and money (the spine), and Middle Tennessee closed it from the builder's side with a 50% rule; new beyond Q90-019's loss.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, signed pledges are enforceable on paper yet colleges very rarely sue and no national statistics exist: the letter makes her figure countable, only the Treasury fund makes it payable.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d and 3e, settles campaign 6 and 11 at source: UNC collects 100% cash (85% by exception) before awarding a contract, so her figure counts toward a contract from January 2033.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d support, Villanova's two thresholds (75% documented pledges, 50% cash): paper counts in 2031, her payout in 2033.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d support, DePauw's firm written commitments for 100% and 75% received, adopted after the 2008-09 crash.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, settles campaign 11: four building rules show paper is necessary and never enough, so first committed in writing, never first cash (D8).
Fri 20 Nov: store and 3d lead-in: the changed-purpose clause gives the receiver the right to redirect, so a founder-led residency names the purpose; excerpt only.
Fri 20 Nov: store; UT's naming waits on payment, default priced in names not lawsuits; naming is not in Laura's plan.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the reliance clause exists because US courts enforce on reliance (Q99); her letter needs no lever to be paid, only to be counted.
Fri 20 Nov: store; pledges, gives, commits as three strengths of promise; a conference sample, not live policy.
Fri 20 Nov: store; a real $5m irrevocable pledge paid over years from future means, the usual shape Laura's one payment from money held reverses.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d lead-in, the letter's parts (figure, facility, January 2033, the late-2032 Treasury fund named as a fund, no condition, late-or-cancelled clause); answers campaign 2's name the instrument; case l.115 risk noted.
Fri 20 Nov: WORDS for 3d: committed or a documented pledge, never secured; keep row 32's guard that no in-writing phrase sits beside the ink image.
Fri 20 Nov: re-read of arts. 406 and 408 in both languages; the substance (only a notarised gift escapes revocation before transfer) is Q83-011 and Q99-028.

Fri 20 Nov: store, at most a 3e clause: art. 418 names no notarised exception, as campaign 2 said; its usual trigger, a giver whose income fell, is what owning first removes; never legal advice (case l.169).
Fri 20 Nov: store only; arts. 416, 417 and 419 draw the line at transfer; no report part needs it.
Fri 20 Nov: store; art. 412's charge is why the letter names the facility; legal background only.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d guard, settles campaign 2's notary suggestion: Taiwanese gift forms read are signed with no notary, so name a signed letter and say nothing about notaries; university forms only.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d opening and 3c bridge; the case's own three jobs (viable, commitment, others' willingness) map to owned, signed, first committed; settles campaign 2, 11 and plain 12 with the case's words.
Fri 20 Nov: 3c to 3d bridge; case l.115's reason (2033 value uncertain) is removed before the meetings, so keep the range and its confidence and say why one written figure follows (D1).
Fri 20 Nov: 3d coherence; the IPS's own verb promise (l.11, l.15) given paper, so the letter adds no step to the frozen plan.
Fri 20 Nov: settles campaign 15 at source: CASE splits what the donor still controls from what is documented, not price; Q11b-032's floor-and-top mapping dies; use CASE only for documentation.
Fri 20 Nov: 3b guard, settles campaign 22: the half kept is promised to no one (IPS l.15), so Klein goes in 3b and nothing near Laura's words; Klein from store Q5c-015, not re-read.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d's sentence for D8: no signature protects a funder from a giver whose means turn, only money already owned does; owned is why it is paid, signed is why it is counted.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d's one parallel (D6 budget), answering plain reader 12: holding money first changed what Middle Tennessee and Spelman did; told about institutions, never casting co-sponsors as unreliable.
Fri 20 Nov: WORDS and CONCEIT guard: the letter is paper and the ink is the Treasury holding; payee the residency, never its legal form; currency named (D9).
Fri 20 Nov: 3b and 3e, settles campaign 5 at source in Chinese: the Ministry's venue capital rule pays a design change inside the original budget and any excess is the grantee's.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e support; the same may-not-ask-for-more rule now on a capital venue grant, with instalments capped at the approved sum; Q11e-016 and Q11d-007 hold the phrase.
Fri 20 Nov: 3b and 3e aha that settles campaign 5 at source: Taiwan's grant follows the settled cost down at its ratio and never above the approved sum, so overruns are never shared pro rata.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e support; two more current Ministry rules recompute the grant downward at the original ratio, so the asymmetry is standing practice; running and emergency grants, not buildings.
Fri 20 Nov: 3b, the exact reply to pro rata: contingency inside the budget is shared in proportion, nothing above it; Keel reading of rule text, labelled so.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d clause drawn against the building's milestones (campaign 24): museum grants pay 30/40/30 at real progress; 30/40/30 itself is Q11e-016's; revision date UNVERIFIED.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e support; Taiwan's 2026 venue rule pays only after the contract is let, so the first bills are met by money already held.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, settles campaign 5 in plain English: Arts Council England will not increase the grant if the organisation spends more.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 3: a capital funder expects the owner to name its overrun route early (contingency, redesign, phasing, new gifts), never the founder's flexibility in words to co-sponsors.
Fri 20 Nov: store; ACE guarantees later instalments only while it has funds, as Taiwan's depend on the legislature; contrast only, never a slight on a named funder.

Fri 20 Nov: 3b reason who paid after US arts buildings; drop in a small residency Laura is the board (governance is outside the case, and D10 puts larger overruns on the residency, never on her); pages approximate.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, why a late building is the base case: Set in Stone's seven to nine years from proposal to opening, beside Q145's 3-9 years late in Taiwan.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of Q200-009 (UNC's 100% cash, 85% by exception), which also carries the bridge-loan interest.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e aha candidate: UNC collects early so interest partly shields against construction inflation; fix: never the plan's own reason for buying the late-2032 fund (the IPS buys it to own the floor before stating it, l.13, l.15); say the rules rhyme, and its interest is in US dollars against a Taiwan index.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; bridging a late pledge has a price (UNC's blended rate, Arizona's bridge funding), and a bridge comes back; terms of a founder's bridge are out of scope.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of Q200-010 (Villanova's 75% pledged and 50% cash).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e support; Arizona expects full cash funding before construction and caps pledge collection at four years; excerpt read.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of Q200-006 (Spelman's quote and Lehman's $3m of $10m); the 2-5% is H7-070's.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e kind of shortfall (campaign 6): flexibility closes a 5% leak on about $424,000 of pledges; Keel arithmetic on a share-return model, not in NUMBERS, so register before print and give the kind first; campaign size is out of scope.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, settles campaign 6 with a scale: the mean 2026 artist-village grant ($37,453, NUMBERS 8d) is 1.8 times her flexibility, so one lost funder exceeds it; running money, a comparison of scale only.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, IPS l.15's third use read honestly: a bridge for a late gift comes back, a lost funder's replacement does not; never named to co-sponsors (Q22-038).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e limit for campaign 24 (in dollars it waits, in buildings it does not); register in NUMBERS before print, and state tails from overlapping windows as the worst of about N independent spans (D7), never 1 in 20 from 3-9-year windows since 1991.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e store; how often a delay outran her flexibility; Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS, overlapping windows (D7 wording), and the half kept is itself still shares after 2033.

Fri 20 Nov: store; bills set the median cost of waiting, the currency the tail; today's 4.19% bill against the 3.0% central cost rise is one day's arithmetic, never a forecast; D7 wording for any tail.

Fri 20 Nov: 3b sentence for campaign 5 and D9-D10; fix: the about 25% is her flexibility plus anything above the top ($28,682, 24.9%, NUMBERS 8u), her flexibility alone is 18.4%, so say dollars first and tie the quarter to the right subject; keep if shares earn the 7.5% assumed.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d currency clause, settles professor 10: every capital grant read is fixed in its own money; her figure is in US dollars and the flexibility keeps her gift's NT$ value by choice (IPS l.15).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, settles plain reader 15 (gentle and hard test in one place, who carries the rest); fix: drop 99.74 in 100 (D7: no model odds rarer than about 1 in 100) and give the joint tail as the worst of about 17 independent two-year spans (D7).

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the case names other sources for remaining facility cost; fix: whose business income is a reading, and drop the same years an overrun or a lost funder is likeliest (D4: can, never a measured link).
Fri 20 Nov: 3d clause shape: Washington pays up to 33% of each invoice on reimbursement and never in advance, the shape for her draws.
Fri 20 Nov: Table 3 note: a building-start watch from 2031 beside row 7, payout in the short-term Treasury ETF until the first draw; a watch, not a third reason to change (IPS l.17).
Fri 20 Nov: 3d citation fix for D11: the prerequisites sentence is Katie Oman's GIA Reader essay (2018), never a Grantmakers in the Arts statement, and its subject is the organisation's own books.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a aha in funders' words: the building eats the running money, and the plan walls the ten off; fix: five of the ten are iBond fund shares, so say Treasuries and Treasury funds, never Laura's ten are in Treasuries.
Fri 20 Nov: store; funders read upkeep as a running cost in the pro forma; the residency's forecast is outside the case.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d support (D11 names Kresge 2008): exact words correct the attack's paraphrase: self-reported, about cover for a crisis; Q51-004 held a near quote.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d clause, Kresge's bridge from campaign to annual fund is when her payments fall due; fix: most of each payment owned from January 2027, all ten from January 2028 (NUMBERS 8u), never owned from Jan 2027 for the ten.
Fri 20 Nov: settles campaign 21 and professor 18 at source: Gneezy's overhead was the cost of asking, not of running, so SD-2 and Q22-029 leave 3d (D11).
Fri 20 Nov: store; the letter doubled how many small donors gave; fix the arithmetic: overhead and seed averaged about $27-28, the control about $24 ($8,040 / 336), not $27-28 in each.
Fri 20 Nov: 3.0 and 3d, settles campaign 10 with the case's own words: $50,000 toward operating expenses, reliable support for its early operations; never covers the decade.

Fri 20 Nov: 3.0 and 3d yardstick: $50,000 is a third to all of a small residency's running costs today; Keel arithmetic on store rows, one yardstick at most, never an estimate of her residency's costs.
Fri 20 Nov: register fix for campaign 10: the NT$14m is Hong-Gah Museum's 2003 running cost, not a residency; drop it as a yardstick, the conclusion stands.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e limit; the fixed base buys about 87% in 2033 and 70% in 2042 of today's $50,000 at 2.4% (matches NUMBERS 8d's $43,368 and $35,032); US prices, house inflation input.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d background; large US foundations gave 32% of arts dollars as operating support and 12% as capital in 2023; US only, 30% unclassified.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, what is rare is the term: operating money fixed for years and already held (12.4% multi-year operating), matching Taiwan's one-year votes; two datasets, Keel synthesis.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d ask: building money is the scarce co-sponsor ask; fix: first committed in writing, never first money (D8, campaign 11).
Fri 20 Nov: 3d funders' rule for D11: a capital funder will not pay regular operating activities yet asks for the project's impact on future operations.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d; funders label every source committed, pledged or projected and test need, so her ten sit in the top class and the word is base.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d, the point SD-2 wanted carried by funders' rules (capital excludes running costs; Taiwan pays repairs first and votes running money yearly); not proof co-sponsors give more.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d wording; covers the decade invites why do you need us, a base shows strength and need; evidence is Q22-038 and Q135-016.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d; Oman's prerequisites are the residency's books, where her Treasuries do not appear, so the ten need a written dated commitment; how it is booked UNVERIFIED.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d clause, why years ahead in funders' words (why give money if the project is complete; three to five years; Kresge's bridge); extends Q11b-025.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Kresge itself added operating support and working capital to its capital work in 2008.
Fri 20 Nov: 3d order, settles campaign 16: purpose first (case l.77-80), her owned commitment as proof, then the ask (building and programmes).

Fri 20 Nov: 3d candidate words; fix: The Treasuries that pay all ten are already mine calls five iBond fund shares Treasuries, so say Treasuries and Treasury funds, and already mine holds only from January 2028; writers test it in Laura's voice.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, settles bond attack 5's pension half at source: the regulator called 2022 short-term liquidity pressure, not a funding problem; the promises held, the cash around them ran short.

Fri 20 Nov: 3a or 3e aha: the government said the DB promise does not depend on the performance of the fund; Laura's rests on nothing else, hence the zero-interest standard; read in a search extract, check the page before quoting.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e guard: industry statements support benefits not at risk, never every member was paid (no census exists).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; LDI funds borrowed through repo and swaps on top of gilts; Laura buys every holding with her own deposit and borrows nothing.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; a solvent scheme was still asked for cash; an unborrowed iBond fund asks nothing of her and its worst case is a lower payout (NUMBERS 3); prospectus not re-read.
Fri 20 Nov: store; pooled LDI funds were hit hardest; her five funds are pooled but unborrowed.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 3; settlement takes three to four working days, against her slack of about 17 days (funds) to 320 days (NUMBERS 8h).
Fri 20 Nov: store; for a borrowed fund speed is a cash call; for Laura neither speed nor size touches the payments once bought.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the Pension Protection Fund kept a cash buffer and sold nothing.
Fri 20 Nov: store; 2022's losses fell on hedges sold low and on employers' cash, not on pensions.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the rescue was of a market; submission author UNVERIFIED.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e accuracy: selling went on to 14 Oct into the Bank's backstop; nothing failed because a rescuer arrived.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the Bank bought only at distressed prices, £19.3bn over 13 days; the profit is UNVERIFIED.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; borrowed funds now need a buffer of about 250bp, her ladder needs none because a rise asks her for nothing; clears Q3b's UNVERIFIED 300-400bp.
Fri 20 Nov: Table 3; of the FPC's three tests only operations applies to her (the custody route for fund payouts, the trade days).
Fri 20 Nov: 3e, settles bond attack 5's SVB half in the joint statement's words: depositors protected, shareholders and some unsecured lenders not.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; the systemic-risk exception is a vote of two boards and the Secretary, and no one would vote to rescue a residency; IPS l.11's anybody else's money.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e aha: the deposit promise was kept with other banks' money, about $16.7bn in special assessments on about 114 banks (quote with its date); the case gives Laura no one to send the bill to.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e; SVB's bonds were low credit risk and would have paid, the loss was in time; Laura's money arrives before her claim.
Fri 20 Nov: Table 3; owned is not available: SVB could not move collateral from its custody bank in time, so test the custody route for a fund payout before December 2032.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e clause; SVB's maturity transformation is the reverse of her plan, where every holding pays out before the payment it is for.
Fri 20 Nov: store; SVB's repair was more selling and borrowing; only the borrowing plan is new beyond Q3b.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 or conceit clause, the Fed lent against Treasuries at par; fix: par holds for the five bonds held to maturity, the five funds pay net asset value (IBTM prospectus, D2), so never Laura's par for all ten.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e control-group candidate ($620bn of paper losses, failures only where money could leave); UNVERIFIED, read the FDIC speech of 6 Mar 2023 at source before use.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e illustration of price risk held to date; Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS, and a 30-year gilt move is not a parallel US shift: register in NUMBERS or drop.
Fri 20 Nov: 3e aha: 2022's funds broke on a rise, Laura's one rate risk is a fall before she buys, ending January 2028 (NUMBERS 1); name 3.89 as the ladder alone and 3.57 with the standard.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 4: the one outside party who can turn a holding into cash early is a fund sponsor (up to $4,589 short at zero cash, NUMBERS 3); so no lender and no depositor can make her sell.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, the disanalogy that answers bond attack 5: an employer, a central bank or other banks stood behind the promises that held; nothing stands behind hers, so each is held where none is needed.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e wording replacing pack C's reserve; fix: each payment sits in a Treasury or a Treasury fund paying out before its date (five are iBond funds paying net asset value), never a Treasury for all ten; SVB once, never Orange County.
